proposals.observation: The blog post "Why do I freeze when I've got too many money decisions to make at once?" published today and is the freshest content in the window. The quiz shows 1 session that loaded the intro and stopped, 1 that reached the email step and stopped, and 0 completions. The blog is the most likely warm-traffic entry point right now, but there is no data showing a call-to-action inside it pointing toward the quiz. Getting today's reader from the freeze post into the quiz is the shortest path between existing content and an email capture.
proposals.proposal: Add a contextual in-body call-to-action near the end of the freeze post, before any existing sign-off, that names the quiz and ties it directly to the decision-paralysis content the reader just consumed. The CTA must pass the Sultanic test: it cannot be something any coach could write. It needs to reference the specific cognitive load pattern the post describes, in Joel's voice. No em dashes, no binary contrast, no fragment stacks.

It maps the specific money script running underneath your decisions, which is a different question from "am I saving enough." Joel built it from Klontz Money Script research and his own intake notes from clients who came in saying they were disorganised and left realising they were afraid. proposals.impact: lifts 37.5% open rate closer to vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends. The Money Vigilance automation hits 66.67% on 12 sends, and Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% on 19 sends. Money Worship is underperforming by a meaningful margin relative to both peers. Subject line is the single highest-leverage variable for open rate and is a one-line file change. The content or length of the sequence may also be a factor, but subject line is the right first hypothesis because it is cheapest to test and reversible.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of Email 1 in the Money Worship automation. The current subject line is unknown but the open rate suggests it is either too generic or too comfortable for readers who scored high on money worship, who tend to be people proud of their earning identity. A subject line that names a specific, slightly uncomfortable truth about that pattern, without hype or jargon, is more likely to get opened by that profile. The new line should feel like something only someone who studied this script closely would write.
proposals.new_text: You scored high on money worship. Here is what that actually costs you.

Fred cannot edit workflow files (blocked path), but Fred can write a visible warning into the README or a monitoring note file that Joel checks daily, so the failure surfaces in human review rather than disappearing into CI logs.
proposals.proposal: Add a FAILED_RUNS_MONITOR.md file at the repo root (not under .github/workflows) that Joel can check each morning as a 30-second manual log review habit. The file explains what to look for in the Actions tab, names the two workflows that failed, and gives a plain-language description of what each failure likely means for the business that day. This is additive, creates no risk to existing code, and costs Joel under a minute per morning until the CI alerts are wired properly.
proposals.new_text:
# Workflow Failures: What to Check Each Morning

Two automated workflows failed on 2026-05-27. Until CI alerting is wired to email or Slack, check the Actions tab in GitHub each morning before 09:00. Look for any run marked with a red cross.

**Daily Blog Post** (failed 07:13 on 2026-05-27)
This workflow publishes one post from the queue each morning. When it fails, no post goes live that day. The queue currently holds 12 posts, so a single failure does not empty it, but three or four consecutive failures will stall top-of-funnel content entirely. If you see this failed, trigger a manual re-run from the Actions tab, or publish the next queued file directly.

**Funnel-Hack Digest** (failed 11:59 on 2026-05-27)
This workflow generates the competitive research digest. A failure here does not affect live traffic or email sends, but it means the digest for that day is missing from your review record. Note the gap in your research log if you use those outputs for content planning.

Check takes under 60 seconds. Green across the board: nothing to do.
